title: Suspension of Licence for Up to Two Years

content.scenario: A food manufacturer was convicted for the first time for selling adulterated products. The court is considering suspending the manufacturer's licence.
content.outcome: The court may suspend the manufacturer's licence for a period up to two years, as it is the first conviction. However, if the manufacturer is convicted again, the court may cancel the licence.

user_queries: What is the maximum period for which a licence can be suspended for a first conviction?
Can a licence be cancelled for a first conviction?
What are the consequences of a second conviction for selling adulterated products?
